title: A Matter of Adjustment
text: We paid a visit to a treatment facility in Zeltoble. Since this place was truly a melting pot of races, it seemed there was even a treatment facility specializing in demi-humans. I paid a bit up front and got Big Sister’s friend admitted for treatment, I say. That was at least one weight off my mind. Big Sister was examined as well. After confirming that Big Sister and the others were resting soundly in the hospital room, Father came to question me in a separate room.
“Still, that was a horrifying thing to witness.”
“Indeed.”
“So… what exactly is the relationship between us and those kids?”
“That’s Big Sister, who was your right hand back in the first world, I say.”
“She was that reliable? Even though she’s so young…”
Father’s doubt was reasonable enough. Even I had only ever known Big Sister in her grown form from the very start, after all.
“She does grow up to be quite splendid, but it seems she goes through a great deal before that happens. Her friend passes away, and it’s after that despair that she meets you and grows, I say.”
“It’s no wonder she’d die in that weakened state. I’m glad we got to her in time.”
“Only… by the time of the Waves, her parents had already died, and the surviving villagers were caught in a slave hunt, which is how they ended up in their current situation, I say.”
“That’s awful… could it be…”
Father stole a glance at Big Sister and her friend before murmuring.
“I guess it’s good we could use future knowledge to save a friend who was supposed to die.”
“Indeed. For now, prioritizing her treatment would be best.”
Just then… Big Sister came stumbling out of the room and bowed her head to us.
“Um… thank you very much.”
“Raphtalia-chan. Are you going to be all right?”
“I’m still… okay.”

Father gently led Big Sister back into the hospital room, went over to her friend’s side, and seemed to be asking all sorts of questions. That was how the day passed. Meanwhile, I went off to earn some money and secure not only Sakura-chan’s egg but also Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs. Of course, I also met back up with the Filolial-samas waiting at the inn in Melromarc. It seemed the Siltvelt envoy had been in contact with an acquaintance.
The next day, I say.
“Raphtalia-chan. You gave me a scare, screaming like that in the night.”
“Her night terrors are severe. Since it’s a mental issue, treatment will take time, I say.”
Father and I decided to have a talk.
“So, we managed to save Raphtalia-chan and the others, but… what should we do from here?”

Hmm… let’s see. Something different from what I’d done before floated up in my mind. If I wanted to play it safe, I could just suggest peddling to Father and coast along uneventfully until the Queen’s return. Itsuki would be incredibly annoying, but that would resolve things well enough. There’d even be a chance to mercilessly dispatch the Crimson Swine. But that wouldn’t be much different from before. Since I’d been given the chance to loop back to this world for a second time, wasn’t there something more I could do?
“Like… if there are other kids out there like that weakened girl, Rifana-chan, who might be on death’s door, I want to save them as soon as possible if we can…”
“Even I don’t recall the whereabouts of every single one of Big Sister’s friends, I say. From what I understand, they’ve been sold off as slaves to all sorts of places.”

I’d gone around requesting help from monster merchants and the kingdom to gather up Keel and Big Sister’s other friends. But even that was proving quite difficult in the current situation. Still, it wasn’t as though we could simply do nothing.

“Sold as slaves… so would it be faster to ask a slave trader for help? When I first heard the word ‘slave’ from Motoyasu-kun, I thought it was outrageous, but… did the me from the first world work hard to save those kids?”
“That’s how it turned out in the end, I say.”
Father, as it happened, ended up saving the people of Big Sister’s village.
“In that case, buying slaves… might not be such a bad thing after all.”
“Slave trading, is it…”
At that point, the Siltvelt envoy spoke up.
“For Shield Hero-sama to gather slaves is not generally a commendable method, but given the present circumstances, it may well be for the best.”
“Yeah. From what Motoyasu-kun told me, going to Siltvelt would just cause problems, so maybe saving Raphtalia-chan and the others is the right thing for a hero to do.”
“Understood.”
Oh? It seemed Father was about to roll up his sleeves for Big Sister and her friends.
“Then shall we provide the necessary funds?”
“Hmm… I suppose I could get Motoyasu-kun to help, but an unexplained transfer of funds might tip Melromarc off, so that’s a problem.”
“By the way, the Father within the loop attempted peddling, just like the Father from the first world, but ended up doing so much good that it sparked a revolution within Melromarc, I say.”
A bitter experience indeed.
“…So doing too much good is bad too, huh. Guess peddling isn’t such a great method either.”
“Indeed. If possible, I’d like you to avoid peddling, I say.”
I wanted him to try something we hadn’t done before.
“Hmm… is there some other good method?”
“Here’s a thought, I say. When it comes to expertise, ask the experts—let’s consult a monster merchant.”
“Would they really tell us so easily? Feels like they might try to swindle us in some weird way.”
“There happens to be a monster merchant who cooperates with us in every loop, so consulting them should be fine, I say. Though Father did have to put on an act so as not to be underestimated.”
“An act, huh… well, all right, let’s go have a chat then.”
“Understood, I say.”
“I shall accompany you as well.”
“Are we going somewhere? Kuro’s coming toooo?”
“Kuro-chan is coming along too, I see. Then let us be off, I say.”
And so we left Big Sister and the others to mind the fort while we headed to the monster merchant in Melromarc.
We arrived in front of the monster merchant’s tent.
“T-they sell slaves here?”
“Indeed. They also deal in monsters, I say.”
Father swallowed hard and clenched his fists.
“I do recall having heard of this particular slave trading guild.”
The Siltvelt envoy seemed to know of this renowned merchant as well. Well, from what I’d heard, they had connections in all sorts of places, so it was likely a trustworthy establishment.
“Well then, shall we enter, I say.”
“Yaaay.”
I took the lead, going in together with Father, the others, and Kuro-chan.
“Well, well, a new customer, is it? Yes, indeed.”
“Filo-tan. Already accounted for, I say.”
“Yes?”
Oops, out of habit I nearly tried to purchase a Filo-tan. I’d already secured the egg that would become Sakura-chan’s Filo-tan.
“Judging by your appearance and the weapons you carry, would I be correct in assuming you are the Spear and Shield Hero-samas?”
“…Yeah.”
“Hero-sama?”
The Siltvelt envoy checked on Father’s reaction. She didn’t know Father well enough to recognize when he was acting.
“According to what we’d heard, word was that you were heading toward Siltvelt—what business, then, brings you to our humble shop?”

“Heh, word travels fast. Going to Siltvelt and reporting this like some kind of tattletale to get revenge on this country would be no fun at all. I merely pretended to leave the country in order to spite the fools running it.”
“Oh my! Then what purpose do you have in mind? Yes, indeed.”
“You didn’t expect me to just tell you outright, did you? I heard this place deals in slaves—is that true or not?”
“Yes, indeed! Our shop does deal in slaves. Yes, indeed.”
“Then would you mind if I took a look at your merchandise?”
“Understood, yes indeed! Please, allow us to show you our merchandise. Yes, indeed!”
With that, the monster merchant began leading us inside. The peculiar smell within the merchant’s tent assaulted my nose. Slaves were crammed into cages, I say.
